hardVisualRules: Every expanded widget preserves the same colour family as its collapsed/original widget.
Large reading surfaces stay premium graphite; semantic identity appears in borders, headings, icons, rails and restrained tints.
Search fields are neutral grey/silver.
Completed reservation/itinerary/checklist surfaces are silver/slate, not bright semantic colours.
Reservation Add/Edit editor stays the approved sky/baby-blue family regardless of booking type.
Itinerary editor family follows travel type: Standard/Home Visit sky, Motorhome orange, Cruise violet; destination-row colours do not recolour editor shells.
Budget Destination Budgets source and manager stay teal; Add/Edit Destination Budget editor stays sky.
Calendar editor shells remain neutral; exact record details preserve destination plus event-type identity.
Checklist and Vault editors remain neutral even when their source widget uses a semantic colour.
Home Alerts use red/amber/green traffic-light severity; expanded Alerts remain concise and Remove-only.
All interactive controls on approved iPad layouts retain at least 44px effective touch targets.
Home 1024 compact Alerts and Trip Timeline dates must remain fully readable without making Home scroll.
Vault header must mask obsolete baked status text/count/date at both approved iPad widths.
Destination Budget manager summary values must not crop 22px currency glyphs.

Journey History summary-card icon tiles are the benchmark for Booked Reservations and The Vault category icons: category-specific colour, dark inset tile, stronger contrast, consistent size/padding/border/glow; Completed remains silver.
Calendar month days may display up to five dated items and the week row grows vertically before +more is used.
Annual Budget main card is display-only; year-by-year annual budget Set/Edit belongs only inside the expanded Annual Budget manager.
Add Expense and Add Reservation prioritise the entered amount and AUD equivalent over helper text; blanket green is not used as general decoration.
All photographic page headers use one consistent physical height across iPad screens; only image/title/content identity changes.

Within any single visible viewport, top-level widgets/cards visible together must have clearly distinct colour identities; the same or near-same colour may be reused only when those widgets cannot be visible together.
App Health detail cards use distinct visual card identities while their status dots/labels remain semantic green/amber/red; expanded App Health cards preserve their source card identity.
Home is a fixed one-screen command centre: the normal main canvas must not document-scroll or drift; only intentionally expanded modal content may scroll internally.

physicalIpadAcceptance.name: Backup is one full JSON; restore replaces current data only after explicit confirmation.
Launch transitions smoothly from app brand/icon to current country/flag/city without flash/blank/jump.
Phrase Helper audio is easy for Kym to follow; “Where’s the toilet?” normal is noticeably slower and Slow is much slower.
Home is a completely still one-screen command centre: no vertical/horizontal document scroll, swipe drift or rubber-band movement on the main canvas at either approved iPad size.
Booked Reservations category icons use Journey History inset icon-tile benchmark with category-specific colours.
Each day can display up to about five entries before overflow indicator; week/day height grows vertically.
Dense reservations remain readable without crushed text.
Journey History map/year filters remain usable and consistent with the shared offline-map and travel-year filtering rules.
Lower analytics widgets use tight deliberate spacing with no large black gaps.
Category icons use Journey History inset icon-tile benchmark with five distinct category colours.
Locked and unlocked header use unified 230px rhythm.
Unlocked action/status rail stays fully inside header bounds, no bottom cropping.
Privacy/lock status is obvious and no sensitive content leaks while locked.
PIN optional; three-tap/unlock flow behaves as approved.
Attachments/screenshots are understandable and usable offline.
Backup/restore requires explicit replace-data confirmation and is safe.
